service.name: app-server-multi-transport-listen-surface
service.what: The app-server accepts a `--listen` URL parsed into `Stdio` (default), `UnixSocket { socket_path }`, `WebSocket { bind_address }` or `Off`. Stdio is newline-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout with a dedicated reader task and writer task; the Unix control socket lives in a private socket directory, is created with mode 0600 and removed by a Drop guard, and each accepted connection is upgraded to a WebSocket. Concurrent app-server starts are serialised by an exclusive `flock` on `app-server-startup.lock`, and a stale control-socket file is detected and unlinked before bind.
invariants: A non-loopback websocket bind must never be created without an auth policy (constructor returns InvalidInput).
Stdio, Unix-socket and raw WebSocket connections must share the identical framed JSON-RPC surface so per-connection state stays transport-agnostic.
constants: control socket accept retry sleep = 1 s

service.name: websocket-listener-authentication
service.what: Non-loopback app-server WebSocket listeners require an explicit auth mode: `capability-token` (a bearer token compared as a constant-time SHA-256 digest, sourced from a token file or a precomputed hex digest) or `signed-bearer-token` (an HS256 JWT validated against a shared secret file with optional issuer/audience match and an explicit clock-skew window). The policy is applied at HTTP upgrade time, and every request carrying an `Origin` header is rejected with 403 before reaching the upgrade handler. Unauthenticated `/healthz` and `/readyz` 200 handlers are also served.
invariants: Capability comparison must stay constant-time (`constant_time_eq_32`); never short-circuit on the raw token.
A `signed-bearer-token` secret shorter than 32 bytes must be rejected at policy construction, not at request time.

service.name: connection-initialize-handshake-and-capability-gate
service.what: Each connection must send `initialize` before any other request; session state is stored once in a `OnceLock<InitializedConnectionSessionState>` holding `experimental_api_enabled`, opted-out notification methods, client name/version, `request_attestation` and MCP extensions. Requests whose protocol type reports an `experimental_reason()` are rejected with 'requires experimentalApi capability' unless the connection negotiated it, and the same negotiation gates outbound traffic. A per-connection `ConnectionRpcGate` closes on disconnect so queued handlers cannot start while in-flight handlers drain, and shutdown awaits every gate.
invariants: `initialize` must be handled before dispatch and must panic if it reaches the initialized dispatcher.
A closed RPC gate must drop queued handlers without polling them, while letting already-acquired handlers finish.

service.name: outbound-backpressure-and-overload-control
service.what: Each connection owns a bounded outbound queue; when the queue fills, the connection is treated as slow and actively disconnected (WebSocket connections get 32K headroom because they legitimately burst, stdio gets 128). On the inbound side a full transport-event queue answers JSON-RPC requests with a distinct overload error `-32001 'Server overloaded; retry later.'` instead of blocking, while responses and notifications fall back to awaiting capacity so they are never dropped; serialization failures become `-32603` errors keyed to the original request id. Broadcast notifications only reach connections that have completed `initialize`.
invariants: Inbound responses must never be dropped when the event queue is full — only requests may be rejected with the overload error.
A broadcast notification must never be delivered to a connection that has not completed initialize.

service.name: remote-control-relay-session
service.what: The app-server can dial out to the ChatGPT backend and serve remote clients when no local transport is configured; enrollment/pairing is persisted in the sqlite state runtime and gated by a `RemoteControlPolicy` derived from managed requirements plus state-db availability. Relayed JSON-RPC is carried as client/server envelopes keyed by (client_id, stream_id) with monotonic seq ids; messages larger than the segment target are split into base64 chunks and reassembled under hard size/count caps, and a bounded outbound buffer retains unacked envelopes so a reconnect can resume from the subscribe-cursor header. Reconnects use exponential backoff that resets after hitting the cap, with websocket ping/pong keepalive and a client tracker that closes idle clients.
invariants: Segmentation must be bounded in count, per-chunk size and reassembled size; a malformed or over-cap chunk is dropped, never buffered unbounded.
The persisted enrollment row and the websocket connect must share one selected server so pairing and connecting cannot race to replace different rows.
constants: REMOTE_CONTROL_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3; ping interval 10 s; pong timeout 60 s; reconnect backoff cap 30 s; connect timeout 30 s; connection shutdown timeout 5 s
Feature::RemoteControl (key 'remote_control') is Stage::Removed, default false (features/src/lib.rs:1474-1479) — the relay that exists is gated by the managed-requirement policy, not this flag

service.name: mcp-server-stdio-endpoint
service.what: `codex mcp-server` exposes Codex itself as an MCP server over newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdio, dispatching ListTools/CallTool/Prompt requests through `rmcp` types and exposing a `codex` tool (plus `codex-reply`) whose input schema is generated from the tool-call parameter type and whose output carries `{threadId, content}`. Approval flows are surfaced as MCP elicitation requests (exec approval and patch approval) that deserialize into a `ReviewDecision` and are submitted back as approval ops; a response that cannot be awaited or deserialized becomes a denial. The process refuses to start when workload identity is selected.
invariants: Stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC frames; all logging and telemetry must go to stderr.
An approval response that cannot be awaited or deserialized must become a denial, never an allowance (mcp-server/src/exec_approval.rs:126-133).
A pending server-to-client request id must be removed from the callback map exactly once; an unknown id must only warn (mcp-server/src/outgoing_message.rs:42-80).

service.name: app-server-schema-and-sdk-contract-export
service.what: The app-server wire contract is generated from the Rust protocol types into TypeScript and JSON Schema with two disjoint export sets (stable and experimental), embedded as zstd-compressed precomputed bundles so tooling can emit the exact contract without a full schema run. Checked-in `schema/typescript` and `schema/json` fixture trees are regenerated wholesale (stale artifacts deleted) and diffed, and the JSON export deliberately excludes the raw-response notification methods while keeping only InitializeParams/InitializeResponse in the v1 allowlist.
invariants: Generated TS must carry the GENERATED_TS_HEADER marker and is never hand-edited.
Stable and experimental export sets must stay disjoint so an experimental type cannot leak into the stable contract.

service.name: headless-jsonl-exec-surface
service.what: `codex exec` is a non-interactive entrypoint that streams the same turn stream as JSONL to stdout when `--json` (alias `--experimental-json`) is passed, via a dedicated event processor that serializes each event with `serde_json` and prints one object per line; a separate human-readable processor renders the same stream as prose. The CLI surface includes `--output-schema <FILE>` to constrain the model's final response, `--output-last-message`, `--ephemeral`, `--ignore-user-config`, `--ignore-rules`, `--skip-git-repo-check`, `--thread-source` and `--strict-config`, and image inputs are passed with `--image`.
invariants: The JSONL stream must be one complete serialized event per line — a serialization failure falls back to an error object rather than a partial line (exec/src/event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs:103-110).
Stdout carries only the event stream in JSONL mode; human-readable mode is a separate processor, so the two cannot interleave.
constants: serialize failure fallback unwraps to a JSON error object (exec/src/event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs:107-110)

service.name: sandbox-helper-and-arg0-dispatch
service.what: One binary serves several privileged helper roles by dispatching on argv[0]: `arg0` resolves the install layout and re-execs itself as the apply-patch helper, the Linux sandbox helper, the Windows sandbox helper, the filesystem helper and (on Unix) the `codex-execve-wrapper`, holding an exclusive `.lock` while it does so. This is what makes `sandbox-exec`/`bwrap`-style confinement and `apply_patch` usable without shipping separate binaries, and the helper paths are derived from the install context rather than from PATH.
invariants: Arg0 dispatch must be resolved from the install context and the current executable, never from a PATH lookup, or a planted binary could take over a privileged helper role (arg0/src/lib.rs:6-31).
The dispatch lock must be held while a helper role is being established (arg0/src/lib.rs:24).
constants: Helper arg1 constants: CODEX_CORE_APPLY_PATCH_ARG1, CODEX_ARG0_EXEC_HELPER_ARG1, CODEX_FS_HELPER_ARG1, CODEX_LINUX_SANDBOX_ARG0, CODEX_WINDOWS_SANDBOX_ARG1 (arg0/src/lib.rs:7-15)

retrieval.name: two-phase-memory-pipeline-with-lease-queue
retrieval.what: Memory generation runs as a fire-and-forget startup task gated on `Feature::MemoryTool`, a non-ephemeral session and a root (non-subagent) source. Phase 1 claims per-thread stage-1 jobs from the memories SQLite DB under a lease, runs extraction prompts with a strict JSON output schema over a secret-redacted, developer/AGENTS.md-filtered rollout transcript at bounded concurrency, and commits under an ownership token. Phase 2 takes a single global consolidation lock with a heartbeat, syncs the selected stage-1 outputs into a git-backed `memories` workspace, diffs against the baseline to decide whether to run a consolidation agent at all, and resets the workspace baseline only after re-confirming the lease. Retention pruning never deletes rows flagged for phase 2. `Feature::MemoryTool` is `Stage::Stable` with `default_enabled: false` (features/src/lib.rs:984-989), so the pipeline is OFF by default.
invariants: Stage-1 retention pruning must never delete rows with selected_for_phase2 = 1 (state/src/runtime/memories.rs:412).
The Phase 2 workspace baseline may only be reset while the worker still owns the job lease; a failed heartbeat aborts the commit (memories/write/src/phase2.rs:437-461).

The consolidation agent must never recursively generate memories: its derived config forces ephemeral=true, generate_memories=false, use_memories=false and disables Collab/MemoryTool/Apps/Plugins/SkillMcpDependencyInstall (memories/write/src/phase2.rs:322-336).
constants: DEFAULT_MEMORIES_MAX_ROLLOUTS_PER_STARTUP = 2; MAX_ROLLOUT_AGE_DAYS = 10; MIN_ROLLOUT_IDLE_HOURS = 6; MIN_RATE_LIMIT_REMAINING_PERCENT = 25; MAX_RAW_MEMORIES_FOR_CONSOLIDATION = 256; MAX_UNUSED_DAYS = 30

retrieval.name: memory-read-tool-family-with-citation-feedback
retrieval.what: A `memories` tool namespace exposes `list` / `read` / `search` / `add_ad_hoc_note` plus a developer-instructions read-path prompt built from `memory_summary.md` and truncated to a token budget. The local backend walks the memory tree rejecting symlinks and hidden paths, matches queries as case-insensitive literal substrings in several modes, and returns context lines with a numeric cursor. Assistant output carries hidden citation blocks that are stripped from visible text and parsed into memory citations, which are written back to the memories DB as stage-1 usage so long-unused memories become prunable.
invariants: Memory read tools must not mutate the tree; only add_ad_hoc_note writes (ext/memories/src/lib.rs:18-22).
Symlinked entries are rejected or skipped so a memory search cannot escape the memory root (ext/memories/src/local/search.rs:49, :116-118).
Cited rollout ids must be deduplicated per citation and resolve to real thread ids before usage is recorded (memories/read/src/citations.rs:22-51).
constants: MEMORY_TOOLS_NAMESPACE = "memories"; tool names add_ad_hoc_note / list / read / search (ext/memories/src/lib.rs:18-22)

Requires `memories.dedicated_tools` to register the tools; MemoriesConfig defaults dedicated_tools=false, use_memories=true, generate_memories=true (config/src/types.rs:339-345; ext/memories/src/tools/mod.rs:40-78)

retrieval.name: reverse-jsonl-tail-scanner
retrieval.what: A read-only scanner reads newline-delimited JSON records backwards from a byte offset, filling a 64 KiB buffer chunk by chunk and reversing each record before deserializing into a caller-supplied type. It can skip records larger than a configured byte limit without buffering or parsing them, and a `new_at()` constructor lets a caller freeze the logical end so records appended after a prefix was captured stay invisible. Invalid JSON is reported as a rejected outcome that leaves the scanner usable; only I/O failures are hard errors.
invariants: `new_at` must reject an end offset past the physical file rather than reading garbage (rollout/src/reverse_jsonl_scanner.rs:43-50).
Invalid JSON must be reported as ScanOutcome::Rejected and leave the scanner usable; only I/O failures become Err (rollout/src/reverse_jsonl_scanner.rs:68-74).
Oversized records must be dropped without accumulating their bytes (rollout/src/reverse_jsonl_scanner.rs:62-66, :98-102).

retrieval.name: session-index-name-lookup
retrieval.what: Thread display names are persisted in an append-only `session_index.jsonl` under codex_home, where the newest row for a thread id wins. Lookups read the log backwards through the reverse JSONL scanner, and name-to-rollout resolution streams all matching ids newest-first so a rename that never materialised a rollout cannot shadow an older usable session. Deletion rewrites the file through a temp file plus rename under a session-index lock.
invariants: The first row seen for an id while scanning from the end is that thread's current name; older rows must be ignored (rollout/src/session_index.rs:251-259).
Writers must hold SESSION_INDEX_LOCK so append and rewrite never interleave (rollout/src/session_index.rs:58-60, :78-80).
Name resolution must keep walking after a match until an id resolves to a loadable rollout (rollout/src/session_index.rs:194-208).

retrieval.name: rollout-content-search-with-ripgrep-fallback
retrieval.what: Cross-session search over rollout JSONL files shells out to ripgrep with fixed-string, case-insensitive, no-ignore path listing, and JSON-escapes the term so it matches inside serialized JSON lines. When ripgrep is unavailable it falls back to an in-process directory walk that builds a case-insensitive literal regex and, for compressed rollouts, opens them through the compression-aware line reader. Snippets are extracted only from user and agent message text, normalized to single spaces and windowed with leading/trailing context.
invariants: ripgrep exit status 1 with empty stderr means zero matches, not an error (rollout/src/search.rs:95-104).
Search terms must be JSON-escaped before matching raw JSONL lines, or a term with quotes or backslashes silently misses (rollout/src/search.rs:54, :238-241).
Snippets come only from user/agent message text; images and audio contribute no text (rollout/src/search.rs:256-305).
constants: scan page size = page_size * 8 clamped to [256, 2048]

retrieval.name: thread-history-occurrence-search-pagination
retrieval.what: Per-thread occurrence search queries the thread_history SQLite database segment by segment along the resolved rollout lineage, selecting only user-message items and each turn's final agent item. Matching happens in Rust over projected text (markdown flattened with pulldown-cmark so styling markup does not break matches) using a case-insensitive literal matcher that maps lowercase match offsets back to original byte ranges. Results carry UTF-16 snippet highlight ranges and a JSON cursor binding thread id, search term, rollout ordinal and occurrence index.
invariants: A cursor is only valid if thread_id and search_term match the request, so a cursor cannot be replayed against a different query (thread-store/src/local/thread_history/search.rs:275-292).
Only userMessage items and each turn's final agent item are searchable; every other item type is skipped (thread-store/src/local/thread_history/search.rs:111-153, :304-351).
Snippet highlight ranges are UTF-16 offsets and must be computed from the same slicing used to build the snippet (thread-store/src/local/thread_history/search.rs:445-475).
constants: page size must be > 0; empty or whitespace search_term is rejected with InvalidRequest

retrieval.name: fuzzy-file-search-nucleo-session
retrieval.what: A nucleo-backed streaming fuzzy path search spawns a walker thread and a matcher thread joined by a crossbeam channel. The walker uses `ignore::WalkBuilder` with hidden entries allowed, symlinks followed, override excludes, and gitignore scoping tied to real git repositories; results are pushed into nucleo through an injector and re-scored as the query changes. The matcher debounces notifications and emits point-in-time snapshots (matches, total match count, scanned file count, walk-complete) and can compute match indices for highlighting.
invariants: The walker must quit promptly on cancel/shutdown, checked at least every 1024 entries (file-search/src/lib.rs:455-492).

Gitignore rules are only honoured inside a git context; disabling respect_gitignore must turn off git ignore, git global, git exclude, .ignore and parent scanning together (file-search/src/lib.rs:431-447).
limit and threads are NonZero, so a session cannot be constructed with zero threads or zero results (file-search/src/lib.rs:105-133).
constants: matcher TICK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10; idle select timeout = 100 ms

retrieval.name: multimodal-input-snapshot-and-image-budget
retrieval.what: Attachment ingestion normalizes a local path into a validated, portable data URL before the item enters history: `snapshot_local_user_input` reads a bounded number of bytes, classifies the image detail into a resize mode (Original versus ResizeToFit), and rewrites `UserInput::LocalImage` into `UserInput::Image` and `LocalAudio` into `UserInput::Audio` with the correct MIME type. At request-build time `image_preparation` applies a budget: a detail-based mode with 2048 max dimension and 2500 max patches, or a unified budget mode with 6000 max dimension and 10000 max patches; failures are replaced by explicit placeholder text rather than dropped silently, and remote image URLs and `detail: low` are rejected with their own placeholders. The unified budget is gated by `Feature::UnifiedImageBudget`, `Stage::UnderDevelopment`, `default_enabled: false`.
invariants: An unprocessable image must become an explicit placeholder string in the prompt, never a silent omission (core/src/image_preparation.rs:21-27, :82-90).
Local media reads are byte-bounded before decoding — image and audio limits are enforced pre-load (protocol/src/local_media.rs:29, :40).
The unified image budget requires BOTH the feature flag and a model that is responses-lite or supports original image detail (core/src/image_preparation.rs:44-50).
constants: HIGH_DETAIL_LIMITS = { max_dimension: 2048, max_patches: 2500 }; UNIFIED_IMAGE_LIMITS = { max_dimension: 6000, max_patches: 10000 } (core/src/image_preparation.rs:29-36)

ops.name: otel-session-telemetry-and-metric-export
ops.what: Each session owns a `SessionTelemetry` carrying low-cardinality identity metadata (auth mode, originator, session source, model, app version) and an optional OTEL metrics client created with a delta-temporality OTLP or in-memory exporter. It exposes counter/histogram/duration helpers plus structured log-and-trace events (conversation starts, api_request, websocket_connect, sse_event, tool_result, sandbox_outcome, turn_cost, user_prompt) and span attributes for gen_ai token counts. A separate runtime-metrics summary aggregates held metric data and is only readable when the delta manual reader is enabled.
invariants: All metric emission must be no-op-safe when the exporter is absent and must never propagate errors to callers (otel/src/events/session_telemetry.rs:164-222).
Metric tag values must pass sanitization before being attached (otel/src/events/session_telemetry.rs:135-138, :391-413).
Exporter shutdown must run at most once and on a prepared detached thread within a time budget (otel/src/provider.rs:96-110, :157-179).
constants: Span fields: gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.cache_write.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, codex.usage.reasoning_output_tokens, codex.usage.total_tokens

Metric names include codex.tool.call, codex.tool.call.duration_ms, codex.api_request, codex.sse_event, codex.websocket.request, codex.turn.e2e_duration_ms, codex.turn.ttft.duration_ms, codex.turn.token_usage, codex.startup.phase.duration_ms
Feature::RuntimeMetrics key 'runtime_metrics' is Stage::UnderDevelopment, default_enabled FALSE (features/src/lib.rs:972-977) — the runtime summary reader is off by default

ops.name: sqlite-log-database-and-diagnostics
ops.what: Alongside the state databases, a dedicated logs database receives tracing events through a bounded queue with batching: events are buffered up to a queue capacity, flushed on a batch size or a flush interval, and pruned by partition byte and row limits plus a retention window inside the same transaction as the insert. Cross-cutting SQLite telemetry records every open and migrate with a counter and a duration tagged by database kind, phase and an error bucket classified from SQLite extended result codes, and only the first installed process-wide sink wins. A read-only audit API can dump thread rows without migrating or repairing the database.
invariants: Telemetry must never influence database behaviour; a failing sink is absorbed locally (state/src/telemetry.rs:11-18).
Only the first installed process-wide telemetry sink wins; later installs are ignored (state/src/telemetry.rs:24-36).
Log pruning must run in the same transaction as the batch insert so callers never observe inserted-but-unpruned rows (state/src/runtime/logs.rs:49-66).
The audit path must use the read-only pool so it cannot create, migrate or repair the state database (state/src/audit.rs:19-31).
constants: DB_INIT_METRIC = codex.sqlite.init.count; DB_INIT_DURATION_METRIC = codex.sqlite.init.duration_ms; DB_FALLBACK_METRIC = codex.sqlite.fallback.count

ops.name: rollout-trace-event-manifest-bundle
ops.what: A separate high-fidelity trace format records one rollout as a bundle directory containing a manifest, an append-only `trace.jsonl` of schema-versioned raw events with monotonic sequence numbers and wall-clock timestamps, and a `payloads/` directory of pretty-printed JSON payloads referenced by payload ref. The writer keeps no in-memory reduced model; a reducer replays the bundle into a reduced cache written as `state.json`. No-op-capable context handles (thread, inference, compaction, MCP call, tool dispatch, code cell) let hot-path code instrument without forcing trace capture on.
invariants: Payload files are written before the event that references them, so an interrupted replay never points at a planned-but-unwritten payload (rollout-trace/src/writer.rs:97-105).
The writer must tolerate a poisoned mutex so diagnostic events after a panic are not lost (rollout-trace/src/writer.rs:136-141).
The manifest's root_thread_id is mandatory and replay must fail rather than invent a placeholder thread (rollout-trace/src/bundle.rs:22-25).
constants: MANIFEST_FILE_NAME = manifest.json; RAW_EVENT_LOG_FILE_NAME = trace.jsonl; PAYLOADS_DIR_NAME = payloads; REDUCED_STATE_FILE_NAME = state.json
Payload naming raw_payload:{ordinal} -> payloads/{ordinal}.json; event log flushed after every append

ops.name: feedback-upload-with-diagnostic-attachments
ops.what: User feedback is buffered in an in-memory ring of tracing output, tagged through a dedicated feedback-tags tracing target, and uploaded to Sentry as an envelope with synthetic attachments: a logs file, a redacted `codex doctor --json` report produced by running the Codex executable as a subprocess, a connectivity diagnostics text file derived from proxy environment variables, and arbitrary file-backed extras. The upload uses a no-redirect client pool, a bounded timeout, and reserved tags (thread_id, classification, cli_version, session_source, reason) that client-supplied tags can never override.
invariants: Attachments are only included when the caller's consent gate sets include_logs (feedback/src/lib.rs:419-425).
A path-backed attachment read failure must be logged and skipped without failing the upload (feedback/src/lib.rs:656-667).
Reserved tags must never be overwritten by client or captured tracing tags (feedback/src/lib.rs:591-615).

The doctor report is best-effort: a missing executable, timeout, non-JSON stdout or parse failure all skip the attachment and let the upload proceed (app-server/src/request_processors/feedback_doctor_report.rs:34-93).
constants: DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 4 MiB ring capacity; UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECS = 10; MAX_FEEDBACK_TAGS = 64
Attachments: codex-logs.log, codex-doctor-report.json, codex-connectivity-diagnostics.txt, codex-apps-tools-cache.json, codex-app-directory-cache.json, windows-sandbox.log

ops.name: turn-cost-accounting-worker
ops.what: An app-server background worker observes turn lifecycle events (started, response completed, finished/interrupted) and polls the Codex backend for priced per-turn API-key costs under an auth manager. A turn only emits a cost event once the backend reports a priced status and the reported response count reaches the count the worker observed; otherwise it is retried with bounded attempts. Emitted costs become a turn-cost telemetry event carrying turn id, estimated USD, interrupted flag, speed and reasoning effort.
invariants: The worker is only spawned when an OTLP exporter is configured and the provider is OpenAI (app-server/src/turn_cost_worker.rs:88-95).
A cost is only emitted when status is Priced and response_count >= expected_response_count, otherwise the entry is retried (app-server/src/turn_cost_worker.rs:389-410).
The in-flight observation channel is bounded and drops rather than blocking the turn loop, and the worker is cancelled on Drop (app-server/src/turn_cost_worker.rs:24, :96, :121-130).

ops.name: network-proxy-policy-audit-and-attribution
ops.what: The managed network proxy evaluates every connection through a policy request (protocol, host, port, environment id, client address, method, command) and produces a typed decision source (baseline policy, mode guard, proxy state, decider). Final decisions are published to a best-effort audit observer as tenant- and session-free events. A separate trusted-attribution path lets the Linux sandbox bridge prefix a connection with a magic-framed execution token so the proxy binds the connection to a per-execution policy state and rejects unknown tokens or environment mismatches. The feature is gated by `Feature::NetworkProxy`, `Stage::Experimental`, `default_enabled: false`.
invariants: The audit observer must observe without delaying or altering enforcement; notification delivery is best effort (network-proxy/src/network_policy.rs:47-50).
An unknown attribution token or an environment mismatch must be rejected with PermissionDenied (network-proxy/src/attribution.rs:48-71).
Attribution token length must be validated on both write and read against MAX_ATTRIBUTION_TOKEN_LEN (network-proxy/src/attribution.rs:94-100, :123-135).

ops.name: analytics-facts-and-feature-state-metrics
ops.what: Analytics facts are the coarse-grained product telemetry channel, distinct from OTel metrics: turn profile facts, turn token-usage facts, resolved-config facts and app-invocation facts are constructed at turn boundaries and shipped through an analytics events client. Feature-flag state itself is reported as an analytics/Otel counter only when an effective value differs from its declared default, which is what makes the flag table self-documenting at runtime; `Stage::Removed` entries are explicitly skipped so dead flags do not generate noise.
invariants: A feature-state metric may only be emitted when the effective value differs from the declared default (features/src/lib.rs:490-505).
Removed-stage features must be skipped by feature-state emission, so a dead flag cannot reappear in telemetry (features/src/lib.rs:491-494).
Token-usage facts are computed as a saturating difference from a snapshot taken at turn start, so a turn's usage is never negative (core/src/tasks/mod.rs:667-688).
constants: Turn facts: TurnProfileFact, TurnTokenUsageFact, TurnResolvedConfigFact, AppInvocation (core/src/tasks/mod.rs:718-777)
Per-turn histograms emitted for tool calls, token usage by token type, unified-exec running processes, network proxy active, memory read-allowed (core/src/tasks/mod.rs:657-766)

ops.name: in-repo-diagnostics-gauges
ops.what: Short-lived process-local metrics are exposed through a small diagnostics crate of `Gauge`/`GaugeGuard`/`Counter` primitives rather than being routed through OTEL, so hot-path code can track live counts cheaply. They are used for active turns, pending mailbox messages and per-turn tool-call accounting, and appear in the turn metrics emitted at turn end.
invariants: A gauge must be released by RAII guard drop so a panicking path cannot leave a stale count (diagnostics/src/lib.rs, used as `ACTIVE_TURNS.track()` in core/src/tasks/mod.rs:428).
Gauge names are a process-wide flat namespace and must stay unique.

interface.name: event-msg-stream-contract
interface.what: `EventMsg` in the protocol crate is the engine-side event contract a renderer consumes: a serde `tag = "type"` snake_case enum with roughly 90 variants covering turn lifecycle, streaming deltas (agent message, reasoning, plan, exec output), tool and approval surfaces, durable extension state (goal updates, queue changes) and sub-agent activity. A source comment pins a hard design constraint on the wire shape — no field may be optional, because optional types break the extension code-gen — and two variants carry v1/v2 interop renames with aliases. Each event travels with a sibling event id used as the turn id by consumers.
invariants: No EventMsg field may be Optional, because optional types break the extension code-gen (protocol/src/protocol.rs:1282-1283).

The wire tag is `type` with snake_case variant names, and the v1 spellings task_started/task_complete must keep their turn_started/turn_complete aliases for v2 interop (protocol/src/protocol.rs:1284-1287, :1329-1341).
Every EventMsg carries a sibling `Event.id` used as the turn id by consumers (app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:154-157).
constants: ~90 EventMsg variants from Error through SubAgentActivity (protocol/src/protocol.rs:1288-1498)
Two variants carry legacy wire renames with aliases: task_started/turn_started and task_complete/turn_complete (protocol/src/protocol.rs:1331, :1340)

interface.name: app-server-notification-contract-and-capability-negotiation
interface.what: The app-server converts each `EventMsg` into a versioned `ServerNotification` JSON-RPC notification with an explicit wire method string (turn/started, item/completed, thread/goal/updated, skills/changed, ...), declared through a macro with `serde(tag = "method", content = "params")`. Variants and individual fields can be marked experimental, and capability negotiation is per connection: `initialize` accepts an `InitializeCapabilities { experimental_api, request_attestation, mcp_server_openai_form_elicitation, opt_out_notification_methods, extensions }`; any request whose type reports an experimental reason is rejected when the client did not opt in, and outbound notifications with an experimental reason or on the opt-out list are silently skipped for that connection. TypeScript and JSON Schema fixtures are generated from the same definitions.
invariants: A request carrying an experimental reason must be rejected unless that exact connection initialized with experimental_api = true (app-server/src/message_processor.rs:884-888).
Notification suppression is per connection and keyed by the exact serialized method name from opted_out_notification_methods (app-server/src/transport.rs:118-120).

Wire method strings are the contract: changing a variant's method literal is a breaking protocol change, which is why the macro takes an explicit literal (app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs:1556-1582).
constants: Experimental gating convention '<method>' or '<method>.<field>' as the reason identifier (app-server-protocol/src/experimental_api.rs:16-19)
Known oddity recorded in source: experimental_api_enabled is scoped per connection, not per instance (app-server/src/request_processors/initialize_processor.rs:63-68)

interface.name: renderer-notification-routing-and-bounded-replay
interface.what: The renderer consumes `ServerNotification`, not `EventMsg`, and routes each notification to a thread by classifying every variant as Thread(ThreadId), InvalidThreadId, AppScoped or Global. Per-thread events land in a bounded ring buffer with a coalescing and eviction policy that merges consecutive agent-message deltas from the same (thread, turn, item) up to a small byte cap, drops any single delta larger than a larger cap, and evicts from the front until both the length and byte budgets hold. The dispatch point rejects a notification whose thread id does not match the widget's thread before any shared handler state is mutated, and only a short allowlist of notification kinds survives a session rebase.
invariants: A notification whose thread id does not match the widget's thread must be rejected before shared handler state is mutated (tui/src/chatwidget/protocol.rs:9-16).

The replay buffer must stay bounded by BOTH an event count and a total delta-byte budget; eviction is front-first and byte accounting is decremented for every evicted delta (tui/src/app/thread_event_buffer.rs:54-76).
Only HookStarted, HookCompleted, McpServerStatusUpdated and buffered requests survive a session refresh; everything else is dropped on rebase (tui/src/app/thread_events.rs:56-67).

interface.name: screen-mode-and-terminal-capability-detection
interface.what: Screen mode is decided by one function: the `--no-alt-screen` CLI flag always wins and forces inline mode, otherwise the persisted `tui.alternate_screen` setting decides, where `Never` means inline and `Auto`/`Always` both use the alternate screen; the result is pushed into the terminal with a documented no-op `enter_alt_screen()` when disabled. Terminal init refuses to start unless BOTH stdin and stdout are TTYs. Separately, terminal capability detection is a startup probe rather than a guess: a terminal-detection crate classifies the terminal and multiplexer from environment variables, and on Unix the TUI runs a bounded 100 ms probe for cursor position, default colors and keyboard-enhancement support, absorbing any failure into an all-unknown probe with warnings rather than aborting startup.
invariants: --no-alt-screen is an absolute override: the mode function returns false before consulting config (tui/src/lib.rs:1781-1783).
alt_screen_enabled = false must make enter_alt_screen() a no-op rather than a silent partial transition (tui/src/tui.rs:659-661).
A failed or timed-out probe must degrade to a fully-unknown probe, never panic or abort startup (tui/src/tui.rs:459-470).
enhanced_keys_supported must default to false when the probe is inconclusive, so no key binding is advertised that the terminal may not deliver (tui/src/tui.rs:486-488, :526).
constants: AltScreenMode = Auto (default) / Always / Never; config field tui.alternate_screen (protocol/src/config_types.rs:635-648; config/src/types.rs:717-723)
TerminalName has 14 variants including Dumb and Unknown; Multiplexer = Tmux{version} | Zellij{version} (terminal-detection/src/lib.rs:25-71)

interface.name: operator-config-layer-stack-and-requirements
interface.what: Operator-facing configuration is a layered stack consumed by the engine: the config crate resolves a `ConfigLayerStack` over multiple sources and exposes the effective config, while a requirements model can constrain what a lower layer is allowed to set (sandbox-mode requirements, an allowed permission-profile list, required profiles, and deny-read filesystem requirements). Managed or enterprise feature overrides are applied through a separate managed-features path, and cloud-provided configuration entries are sourced and attributed so a value's origin is known. The app-server surfaces a permission-profile catalog derived from this stack, marking each profile allowed or not.
invariants: A requirement must be enforced at catalog-construction time, not at use time, so a disallowed profile is never offered (core/src/config/permission_profile_catalog.rs:45-96).
A constrained value must report its source so an operator can tell which layer imposed it (config/src/lib.rs ConfigLayerStack API; config/src/requirements.rs).
Managed feature overrides must be applied through the managed-features path rather than mutating user config, so they cannot be persisted back (core/src/config/managed_features.rs).
constants: Config crate is 65 source files; the requirements model is 186 lines and the managed-features model 329 lines
A JSON-schema generator exists for the config surface (config/src/schema.rs: 270 lines)
Cloud-sourced config is a separate 9-file crate (cloud-config)

interface.name: slash-command-capability-gating
interface.what: The renderer's command surface is gated by three orthogonal predicates on the `SlashCommand` enum, all evaluated by the backend rather than the widget: `is_visible()` gates platform and build (some commands are Windows-only, macOS/Windows-only, non-Android, or debug-build only) and is the sole filter used by `built_in_slash_commands()`; `available_in_side_conversation()` is an allowlist of the commands valid inside a side conversation; `available_during_task()` restricts the commands valid while a task is in progress, with an exhaustive match forcing a decision for every variant. Feature-driven commands are gated through data rather than a separate menu table, so the resulting list is a pure function of the enum plus cfg.
invariants: `built_in_slash_commands()` must remain a filter over `is_visible()` so no command can be registered without passing the platform/build gate (tui/src/slash_command.rs:278-283).
A command not explicitly listed as available_during_task() must be unavailable while a task runs — the match is exhaustive with explicit true and false arms (tui/src/slash_command.rs:205-263).
`available_in_side_conversation()` is an allowlist: only the listed read-only commands remain valid in a side conversation (tui/src/slash_command.rs:188-202).
constants: Platform gates: some commands windows-only, some macos|windows, one excluded on android, two debug_assertions-only (tui/src/slash_command.rs:266-274)
available_during_task() explicitly denies 24 commands including New, Archive, Fork, Init, Compact, Review, Plan, Clear, Logout (tui/src/slash_command.rs:205-227)

interface.name: selected-capability-roots
interface.what: The backend interface includes a capability-root selection model: a `SelectedCapabilityRoot` pairs a platform-supplied stable id with a `CapabilityRootLocation` that names an execution environment plus an absolute path URI, and the path deserializer accepts either a parsed path URI or a legacy app-path string, so older clients keep working. The selected roots are carried on the session (rollout creation records them) and are what resolves into concrete paths per environment.
invariants: A capability root must carry both an environment id and an absolute path; there is no same-host shorthand (protocol/src/capabilities.rs:12-36).
